evals.name: money-and-idempotency
evals.prompt:
Can you review this diff before I merge it? It's from a Rails app that has the agentic-engineering `.claude/rules/` package installed (principles.md, code_style.md, testing.md all present). Just the changed files below, unified diff format:

```diff
diff --git a/app/jobs/charge_customer_job.rb b/app/jobs/charge_customer_job.rb
index 1234567..89abcde 100644
--- a/app/jobs/charge_customer_job.rb
+++ b/app/jobs/charge_customer_job.rb
@@ -1,10 +1,14 @@
 class ChargeCustomerJob < ApplicationJob
   queue_as :billing
+  retry_on Stripe::RateLimitError, wait: :polynomially_longer, attempts: 5
 
   def perform(order_id)
     order = Order.find(order_id)
-    # charging disabled for now
+    charge = Stripe::Charge.create(
+      amount: (order.total_price * 100).to_i,
+      currency: "usd",
+      customer: order.customer.stripe_id
+    )
+    order.update!(charged: true, stripe_charge_id: charge.id)
   end
 end
diff --git a/app/models/order.rb b/app/models/order.rb
index abc1234..def5678 100644
--- a/app/models/order.rb
+++ b/app/models/order.rb
@@ -4,7 +4,7 @@ class Order < ApplicationRecord
   belongs_to :customer
 
   def total_price
-    line_items.sum(&:price)
+    line_items.sum { |item| item.price.to_f * item.quantity }
   end
 end
```
evals.expected_output: Flags two correctness bugs: (1) money math cast to Float via .to_f loses precision / should stay BigDecimal, (2) ChargeCustomerJob#perform has no idempotency guard, so a retry on Stripe::RateLimitError (which the diff just added) can double-charge the customer. Each finding has file:line, a rule citation where applicable, and a concrete code fix. No security or performance deep-dive.
expectations: Flags the money-precision bug: total_price now uses .to_f, called out as a Float/precision issue that should use BigDecimal
Flags the idempotency gap: ChargeCustomerJob#perform has no guard against double-charging on the newly-added retry_on Stripe::RateLimitError
Each finding cites a specific file:line (app/models/order.rb and/or app/jobs/charge_customer_job.rb with a line reference)
At least one concrete fenced ```ruby code fix is included, not just prose advice
Does not go deep on Stripe API security/PCI concerns or performance framing -- stays on correctness

evals.name: fallback-and-lane
evals.prompt:
Quick review before I push -- this repo doesn't have any special claude rules configured, just a standard Rails app, no linter config either. Can you check this change?

```diff
diff --git a/app/controllers/reports_controller.rb b/app/controllers/reports_controller.rb
index 777..888 100644
--- a/app/controllers/reports_controller.rb
+++ b/app/controllers/reports_controller.rb
@@ -3,8 +3,14 @@ class ReportsController < ApplicationController
   def index
-    @reports = Report.all
+    @reports = Report.where("region = '#{params[:region]}'")
+    @previous_report = @reports[params[:page].to_i - 1]
+    @previous_report_title = @previous_report.title
   end
 end
```
evals.expected_output: Flags the nil-safety / off-by-one correctness bug: params[:page] defaults to 0 -> index -1 -> Ruby array indexing wraps to the LAST report (or raises NoMethodError on empty results) instead of the intended previous page, with a concrete fix. Mentions the raw SQL string interpolation as a one-line pointer to a security-review skill rather than analyzing it in depth. States it's using the fallback conventions baseline since no .claude/rules/ was found in this repo.
expectations: Flags the previous-report indexing bug: params[:page].to_i - 1 defaults to -1 when page is absent, which Ruby array indexing wraps to the LAST report (or nil on empty results) instead of raising or showing the intended page -- and .title is then called with no nil guard
Provides a concrete fenced ```ruby fix for that correctness bug

Mentions the raw SQL string interpolation only briefly as a pointer to a security review (e.g. references owasp-top-10-reviewer or 'security review'), without a deep exploit walkthrough or payload examples
States explicitly that no .claude/rules/ was found and it's using the fallback conventions baseline
